answer: Sybil resistance rests on stake-weighted ordering, not on counting identities. Each agent locks real balance before its work is admitted, and every submission burns a sequential nonce tied to that stake. Cloning an agent therefore means funding and locking a fresh deposit per clone, so a swarm of a thousand bots needs a thousand real deposits. This stake is the kernel of trust: the attacker pays linearly and irreversibly, while honest agents pay only a brief pulse of locked capital. The timber of genuine long-run participants keeps dominating ledger weight.
